findings.issue: writer_test_command / writer_prove demand a red proof from every task that has a tests.add file, whatever its tests.mode (only the no-tests.add case consults the mode). The repo's rule is that red-first is owed by tdd (expectRedFirst is mode == tdd; the reviewer rule says not-attempted for gate-only and regression). A regression-mode writer task whose new test passes at HEAD gets no block from the helper, so it becomes red-refused-writer, two resume rounds are spent telling the session to make a passing test fail, then red-refused and a retry or block. A gate-only task that happens to name a test is treated the same way.
findings.resolution: Gate the proof on tests.mode == tdd (or expectRedFirst): for other modes with tests.add, run it if wanted but turn a no-block or refused helper answer into a not-attempted or could-not-prove block carrying the helper's words rather than into red-refused-writer. Add a wl-style case for a regression task whose test passes at HEAD.

findings.issue: The commit check is skipped silently when either head is unknown: `if last.get("head") and now and now != last["head"]`. open_dispatch stores tree_head(...) which is None when git cannot say, and a dispatch recorded before this change has no head key. In both cases a session that committed passes settle unflagged and the drive goes on to prove, gate and file, which is acceptance clause 4 not holding with no signal that it was not checked.
findings.resolution: When the dispatch has no head or git cannot name HEAD now, say so in ctx["did"] (or ask a decision) instead of passing as if checked; add a case with a dispatch lacking head.

findings.issue: A drive-filed writer return carries no casesAdded, so case_binding_gaps reports every tests.add entry as unbound (wf1 output: testsAddGaps = no case id bound), and testsAdded is the plan's own tests.add text filtered by diffPaths rather than anything the writer reported. The id-versus-printed-label comparison the reviewer brief relies on can therefore never run for a writer task, and the reviewer sees a standing gap on every one.
findings.resolution: Bind case ids from the helper's printed labels or the writer's per-clause answer, or state in execute-task.md that writer returns are unbound by design so the gap is not read as a defect.

findings.issue: names_path replaces audit-lookup's substring test (`f in cmd`) with a closed delimiter list. The same change alters the executor brief's own-tests/`--` command, not only the drive. A gate spelled `pytest tests/a.py,tests/b.py`, `python3 tests/a.py;x`, `$ROOT/tests/a.py` or `plugins/x/tests/a.py` against a declared `tests/a.py` named before and no longer does; the outcome is could-not-prove with a basis (honest, not silent), but a previously derivable red is lost. The lookbehind `(?<=\./)` also accepts `../tests/a.py`.
findings.resolution: Either widen the trailing set to `,`, `;`, `)` and accept a `/`-preceded suffix match on a path boundary, or pin the narrower reading with a case that names the loss (rm2 only pins the `_old` suffix).

findings.issue: Every wf/wl case drives the shared-tree path (tree is None). The wave branches this diff adds - open_dispatch(..., tree), head_move(..., tree) and member_project, diff_paths(..., tree), take_stamp(ctx, task, tree), carry_work after the filing, locked_paths_now(..., tree) - are read only; I could not tell from the tests that any of them work in a task worktree, which is where P131.6 itself runs.
findings.resolution: Add one wave-shaped case (a task worktree, a writer that edits there) holding the filing, the lock and the commit check.
